mainTopic: Animal gear on שבת: extra security as a burden, wrapped versus led chains, and whether animal chains can become טמא
overview: This amud opens at the end of a story. A rider asks whether a wild donkey may go out on שבת in a פרומביא, and the answer is that the הלכה follows חנניה: extra security gear is not a burden. A ברייתא then permits a goat with a hole carved between its horns to go out with an אפסר. רב יוסף asks what happens if the אפסר is tied through the goat's beard, and the question ends in תיקו. Next, רב and שמואל argue about a strap between a cow's horns. After proofs, counter-proofs and a 'remove one tradition' debate, the גמרא concludes that שמואל permits a strap used for guarding and רב forbids it. A challenge from a פרה אדומה tied with reins is answered three ways. The גמרא then explains the משנה's words 'go out' and 'be led'. רב הונא allows a wrapped chain and שמואל does not, and reports from רב הונא's household and רבי's household support wrapped halters, with רב אסי showing why each report is needed. Finally, the גמרא asks whether animal chains can become טמא at all and begins quoting a משנה about rings that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Asking about a wild donkey wearing a halter
steps.stepSummary: The rider decides to ask a halachic question so the other חכם will not feel slighted. He asks whether a badly behaved donkey may go out on שבת wearing a פרומביא.
steps.simpleTranslation: [I'll ask him something] so that he will be calmed. He said to him: A donkey with bad habits, like this one, may it go out with a halter on שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: We are at the end of a story. The rider asks a real הלכה question, partly to show respect to the scholar he met.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A normal donkey only needs a simple bit, so a full halter is 'extra' security. The question is whether extra security turns the halter into a משוי (a burden) that is forbidden to carry out on שבת. Here the donkey is wild, which makes the case harder.

keyTerms.meaning: so that his mind will be settled / so he will be appeased
its conduct is bad (an unruly animal)
a halter or muzzle-type harness
what is the law? (opens a question)

phrases.english: so that he will be appeased.
phrases.notes: End of the rider's thought from the previous part of the story.

phrases.english: He said to him:
A donkey whose conduct is bad, like this one,
what is the law about going out with a halter on Shabbat?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a halter that gives extra security, on an unruly donkey, count as a forbidden burden on שבת?

steps.title: The answer: the law follows חנניה
steps.stepSummary: The answer quotes the questioner's own father in the name of שמואל: the הלכה is like חנניה, who permits extra security gear.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what your father said in the name of שמואל: The law is like חנניה.
steps.whatsHappening: The question gets a direct answer, based on a ruling of שמואל passed down through the asker's own father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חנניה holds that gear which guards the animal more than it needs is still treated as guarding, not as a burden. So the halter is allowed, even on this wild donkey.

keyTerms.meaning: your father
in the name of שמואל
the law follows חנניה (extra security is permitted)

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל rules like חנניה: gear that gives extra security is not a burden. The end of this passage relies on this ruling.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Thus said your father in the name of Shmuel:
The law is in accordance with Chananya.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Permitted, because the הלכה follows חנניה that extra security is not a burden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This same statement of שמואל is used again in step 8 to identify שמואל's view.

steps.title: A goat with a hole carved between its horns
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from the school of מנשיא teaches that a goat with a hole carved between its horns may go out with an אפסר on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in the school of מנשיא: A goat that someone carved a hole for between its horns may go out with a bit on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about goats. It also sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אפסר is threaded through the carved hole, so it is held firmly and will not fall off. Since there is no worry that it will drop and the owner will carry it, it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: it was taught in the school of מנשיא
goat
carved / bored a hole
bit / bridle

phrases.english: It was taught in the school of Menashya:
A goat for which one carved out a hole between its horns
may go out with a bit on Shabbat.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אפסר fixed through a hole between a goat's horns is permitted on שבת because it is secure.

steps.title: What if the bit is tied through the goat's beard?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks about tying the אפסר through the goat's beard instead. He lays out two sides: pain keeps the goat from pulling it off, or the knot may loosen and the bit may fall.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף asked: If he stuck it through its beard, what is the law? Since if it pulls it off, it would hurt, maybe it won't come to pull it off. Or maybe sometimes it loosens and falls, and he will come to carry it ד׳ אמות ברשות הרבים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף takes the ruling from step 3 and asks about a slightly different case. He explains both ways it could go.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: pulling on its beard hurts the goat, so it will leave the bit alone, and the bit is as secure as the horn-hole. Side two: a beard is not as firm as a hole in the horn, so the knot may slip. Then the owner might pick up the bit and carry it ד׳ אמות ברשות הרבים.

keyTerms.meaning: asked (a real dilemma)
inserted / stuck through
its beard
or perhaps (introduces the other side)
loosens and falls
the public domain

phrases.english: Rav Yosef asked:
If he inserted it through its beard, what is the law?

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּאִי מְנַתַּח לַהּ כָּאֵיב לַהּ
phrases.english: Since if it pulls it off, it hurts it,
it will not come to pull it off;
or perhaps sometimes it loosens and falls,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָתֵי לְאֵתוּיֵי אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים.
phrases.english: and he will come to carry it four cubits in the public domain.

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a bit tied through the beard secure enough to permit, like the horn-hole case?

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends רב יוסף's question with תיקו. No answer is found.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes this question without deciding it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither side could be proven. The beard case is left as an open doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: let it stand (the question remains unresolved)

steps.confusionAlert: תיקו does not mean 'permitted' or 'forbidden'. It means the question is left open. Later פוסקים decide how to treat the doubt.

phrases.english: Let it stand [unresolved].

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The beard case remains an unresolved doubt.

steps.title: The משנה about a strap between a cow's horns
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from elsewhere: a cow may not go out with a strap between its horns.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: And not with a strap that is between its horns.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source. This sets up the argument about it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה simply says the strap is forbidden. It does not say why, or whether the reason for the strap makes a difference. The next step debates exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: strap
its horns

phrases.english: We learned there:
And not with a strap that is between its horns.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A cow may not go out with a strap between its horns.

steps.title: רב and שמואל argue about the strap
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה בר אבא reports a dispute. One view forbids the strap whether it is for beauty or for guarding. The other forbids it only for beauty and permits it for guarding.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה בר אבא said: רב and שמואל disagree about it. One said: Whether for beauty or for guarding, it is forbidden. And one said: For beauty it is forbidden, for guarding it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that רב and שמואל explain the משנה differently. It does not yet tell us who holds which view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that a strap worn for looks (נוי) is a burden. The argument is about a strap worn to guard the cow, which is extra security, since a cow does not really need it. One view says even that is a burden. The other permits it.

keyTerms.meaning: they disagree
one said (the speaker is not named)
for beauty / decoration
for guarding / securing

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba said:
Rav and Shmuel disagree about it.

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: בֵּין לְנוֹי בֵּין לְשַׁמֵּר — אָסוּר.
phrases.english: One said: Whether for beauty or for guarding, it is forbidden.
And one said: For beauty, it is forbidden;
but for guarding, it is permitted.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: One view forbids the strap in all cases. The other permits it when its purpose is guarding.

steps.title: רב יוסף proves שמואל is the lenient view
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף shows that שמואל must be the one who permits a guarding strap, because שמואל ruled like חנניה that extra security is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Conclude that it is שמואל who said: for beauty it is forbidden, for guarding it is permitted. For רב הונא בר חייא said in the name of שמואל: The law is like חנניה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף solves the 'who said what' question from step 7. He uses a known ruling of שמואל as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חנניה holds that extra security gear is not a burden. A strap worn to guard a cow is exactly that kind of extra security. Since שמואל rules like חנניה, he must be the one who permits it, and רב must be the one who forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: conclude / it can be determined

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל: a strap for beauty is forbidden, a strap for guarding is permitted (like חנניה). רב: forbidden either way.
steps.whyThisMatters: This links the two sources. שמואל's ruling like חנניה (step 2) decides both the donkey's halter and the cow's guarding strap, since both are extra security.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Conclude that it is Shmuel who said
for beauty it is forbidden, for guarding it is permitted.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: For Rav Huna bar Chiya said that Shmuel said:
The law is in accordance with Chananya.

steps.raayaObject: Which side of the dispute belongs to שמואל
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב הונא בר חייא quoting שמואל: הלכה כחנניה

steps.title: אביי argues the opposite: שמואל forbids even a guarding strap
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that שמואל is the one who forbids the strap in every case. His proof is that שמואל reported a list of animals that go out with a halter, and that list excludes a camel with a nose ring, which is extra security.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: On the contrary! Conclude that it is שמואל who says that the strap is forbidden whether it is for beauty or for guarding. For רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The students swapped the animals' gear before רבי and asked, 'What is the law if one animal goes out with the gear of another?' רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי said before him: 'So said my father: Four animals go out with a halter: the horse, the mule, the camel, and the donkey.' Doesn't this list come to exclude a camel going out with a nose ring?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back against רב יוסף. He says שמואל's own words show that שמואל forbids even a guarding strap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A camel normally needs only a halter. A nose ring holds it more tightly, so it counts as extra security. If the list in שמואל's teaching leaves out a camel with a nose ring, then שמואל treats extra security as a burden, and that clashes with step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary; the opposite is true
Conclude / it can be proven
They swapped (the animals' gear) to ask about it
This animal's gear on that animal
Nose ring (a tighter way to hold a camel)

steps.confusionAlert: The halter is fine for the camel. The question is only about the nose ring. It holds the camel tighter than it needs, and that extra security is what may count as a burden.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: On the contrary,
conclude that it is Shmuel who said
whether for beauty or for guarding, it is forbidden.
For Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
They swapped (the cases) before Rebbi:
What is the law of this one's gear on that one?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לְפָנָיו רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei said before him,
So said my father:
Four animals go out with a halter
the horse, the mule, the camel, and the donkey.
Does this not come to exclude a camel with a nose ring?
phrases.notes: A nose ring is extra security for a camel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: אַדְּרַבָּה, תִּסְתַּיֵּים דִּשְׁמוּאֵל הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Counter-proof to רב יוסף's proof in step 8
steps.raayaObject: שמואל forbids the strap even for guarding
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's report of רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי's list, which excludes a camel with a nose ring

steps.title: Remove this statement in favor of that one
steps.stepSummary: Since שמואל's two statements contradict each other, one of them is set aside. The camel list is removed in favor of the ruling like חנניה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Remove this one in the face of that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The two teachings of שמואל clash. The answer is simply to set aside the camel-list teaching and keep his ruling like חנניה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No attempt is made to reconcile the two statements. One report of שמואל is treated as unreliable, so the original conclusion stands: שמואל permits extra security.

keyTerms.meaning: Remove / take out (from the text or tradition)
In the face of / because of

phrases.english: Remove this one in the face of that one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's contradiction
steps.terutzResolutionType: Removing one of two contradictory traditions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's camel teaching shows he forbids extra security
steps.terutzMaskana: The camel teaching is set aside, so שמואל permits extra security

steps.title: Why remove this one and not the other?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we chose to drop the camel list. We could just as well drop the ruling like חנניה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see that made you remove this one in the face of that one? Remove that one in the face of this one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the choice. If two statements clash, why keep one rather than the other?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing a tradition needs a reason. Without one, the decision is arbitrary, and the camel list could win instead.

keyTerms.meaning: And what did you see? (Why did you choose this way?)

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאי חֲזֵית דִּמְסַמֵּית הָא מִקַּמֵּי הָא?
phrases.english: And what did you see that made you remove this one in the face of that one?
Remove that one in the face of this one!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי חֲזֵית דִּמְסַמֵּית הָא מִקַּמֵּי הָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the choice made in step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: The decision to drop the camel-list teaching
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two clashing traditions carry equal weight unless there is a reason to prefer one

steps.title: A direct report shows שמואל permits a guarding strap
steps.stepSummary: We keep the permissive view because another report says it outright. רב forbids the strap in both cases, while שמואל forbids it for beauty and permits it for guarding.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Because we find that it is שמואל who says: for beauty it is forbidden, for guarding it is permitted. As it was stated:) רב חייא בר אשי said in the name of רב: Whether for beauty or for guarding, it is forbidden. And רב חייא בר אבין said in the name of שמואל: For beauty it is forbidden; for guarding it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains its choice. A clear, explicit report has שמואל permitting a strap used for guarding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are now two sources supporting a permissive שמואל: his ruling like חנניה and this direct report. Against them stands only one source, the camel list, which relies on an inference. So the camel list is the one set aside, and the dispute in step 7 is settled: רב is strict and שמואל is lenient.

keyTerms.meaning: For beauty / decoration
For guarding / securing the animal

steps.whatToRemember: רב forbids the strap whether it is for beauty or guarding. שמואל forbids it only for beauty and permits it for guarding, because he holds that extra security is not a burden.
steps.confusionAlert: The words in parentheses are an explanatory addition in the printed text. They introduce the report that follows.

phrases.english: (Because we find that it is Shmuel who said:
for beauty it is forbidden, for guarding it is permitted.
As it was stated:)

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Chiya bar Ashi said in the name of Rav:
Whether for beauty or for guarding, it is forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: And Rav Chiya bar Avin said in the name of Shmuel:
For beauty, it is forbidden; for guarding, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11's challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either teaching of שמואל could be dropped
steps.terutzMaskana: An explicit report supports the permissive view, so the camel list is dropped

steps.title: Objection from the red heifer tied with reins
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a פרה אדומה stays kosher even if its owner tied it with reins. If extra security counted as a burden, the Torah's rule that no yoke may come upon the heifer would disqualify it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: If its owner tied it with its reins, it is kosher. But if you think it is a burden, the Torah says, 'upon which no yoke has come'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the view that extra security is a burden, which is רב's strict view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A cow usually does not need reins, so reins are extra security for it. If extra security were a burden, the reins would be like a yoke and would disqualify the פרה אדומה. Since the ברייתא says the heifer stays kosher, it seems extra security is not a burden.

keyTerms.meaning: Its reins / lead rope
If it enters your mind (if you were to think)
A burden / load
Yoke (any burden that disqualifies a פרה אדומה)

phrases.english: They challenged: If its owner tied it with its reins, it is kosher.
And if it enters your mind that it is a burden,

phrases.aramaic: ״אֲשֶׁר לֹא עָלָה עָלֶיהָ עוֹל״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא!
phrases.english: the Torah said, 'upon which no yoke has come'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New challenge against the view that extra security is a burden
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that extra security counts as a burden (רב's view)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If extra security were a burden, the reins would disqualify the heifer as a yoke, but the ברייתא says it stays kosher

steps.title: אביי: the heifer was being led from city to city
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the ברייתא is about a heifer being led between cities. In that situation reins are needed, so they are not extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is a case where he is leading it from city to city.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers that the reins in the ברייתא are normal security, not extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal taken away from its familiar place needs to be held more firmly. The reins are therefore ordinary guarding, which is not a burden, so this case does not challenge רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Leading it from city to city

phrases.english: Abaye said: When he is leading it from city to city.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to a special situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The reins are extra security for the heifer
steps.terutzMaskana: While traveling, the reins are needed security, not a burden

steps.title: רבא: a red heifer is valuable, so it needs more guarding
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the heifer is different because it is very costly. Its owner rightly guards it more, so the reins are not extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A heifer is different, because its value is high.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second answer to the objection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike אביי, רבא does not need a travel case. Because a פרה אדומה is so expensive, firm guarding is normal for it, so the reins are not a burden.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different
Its price is high

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא אָמַר: שָׁאנֵי פָּרָה דְּדָמֶיהָ יְקָרִין.
phrases.english: Rava said: A heifer is different, since its value is high.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: שָׁאנֵי פָּרָה דְּדָמֶיהָ יְקָרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Alternative answer to step 13, parallel to אביי's
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case by the animal's special value
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Reins on a cow are extra security
steps.terutzMaskana: For a costly heifer, reins are normal security

steps.title: רבינא: the heifer was rebellious
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says the ברייתא is about a wild, rebellious heifer that needs reins.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: It is a case of a rebellious heifer.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a third answer: the reins were needed because this heifer was hard to control.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rebellious animal needs reins as ordinary guarding. All three answers agree on the same point: in the ברייתא the reins are not extra, so the ברייתא does not prove that extra security is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Rebellious / wild (animal)

steps.whatToRemember: The פרה אדומה case is answered three ways: it was traveling (אביי), it is valuable (רבא), or it was rebellious (רבינא). Each answer makes the reins needed security, so the view that extra security is a burden still stands.

phrases.english: Ravina said: With a rebellious one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third alternative answer to step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to a special animal
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Reins on a cow are extra security
steps.terutzMaskana: For a rebellious heifer, reins are needed security

steps.title: What do 'go out' and 'be led' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a horse with a chain and asks what each of its two verbs means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'A horse with a chain, etc.' What does 'they go out' mean, and what does 'they are led' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting the משנה about animals with chains. It sets up the next move by asking what 'go out' and 'be led' each refer to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses two verbs: animals with chains 'go out' with them and 'are led' by them. If both meant the same thing, the משנה would not need two words. So the גמרא wants to know whether they describe two different allowed ways to use the chain.

keyTerms.meaning: A chain or ring worn around an animal's neck
They go out (into the public domain on שבת)
They are led or pulled (by the chain)
Etc. (the rest of the quoted text is understood)

phrases.english: A horse with a chain, etc.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה. The full line says that all animals that wear chains may go out with them and be led by them.

phrases.english: What is meant by 'they go out'?
And what is meant by 'they are led'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the פרה אדומה's reins and starts on the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'go out' and 'be led' describe two different allowed ways to use the chain, and what each way is.

steps.title: רב הונא: either wrapped or led is allowed
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says the two verbs describe two separate options, and both are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: They may either go out with the chain wrapped around the neck, or be led by it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the question. 'Go out' means the chain is wrapped around the animal's neck, and 'be led' means a person pulls the animal by it. Both are allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב הונא, a wrapped chain still counts as part of how the animal is normally dressed, so it is not a burden. The משנה's two verbs therefore list two permitted options.

keyTerms.meaning: Wrapped (wound around the animal's neck)
Either... or

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
Either they go out wrapped,
phrases.notes: The chain is wound around the neck, not held by a person.

phrases.english: or they are led.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: אוֹ יוֹצְאִין כְּרוּכִין, אוֹ נִמְשָׁכִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Go out' means wrapped and 'be led' means pulled by the chain. Both are permitted.

steps.title: שמואל: led is allowed, wrapped is not
steps.stepSummary: שמואל reads the משנה as allowing only one way: the animal goes out while being led by the chain. A wrapped chain is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: They may go out being led, but they may not go out with the chain wrapped.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a different answer. In his reading, the משנה's two verbs describe one single case: going out while being led. Going out with the chain wrapped is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, a chain wrapped around the neck with no one holding it does nothing useful, so it counts as a burden on שבת. Only a chain that is actually used for leading counts as the animal's gear.

keyTerms.meaning: And they may not go out

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל does not drop the word 'go out.' He reads 'go out, being led' as one phrase describing one allowed case.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
They go out being led,
but they do not go out wrapped.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: יוֹצְאִין נִמְשָׁכִין, וְאֵין יוֹצְאִין כְּרוּכִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer that disagrees with רב הונא's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only leading is permitted. A wrapped chain is forbidden.

steps.title: A ברייתא allows a loosely wrapped chain
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא permits the chain to be wrapped as long as it stays loose enough for the animal to be led by it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: They may go out with the chain wrapped, so that it can be used to lead them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. It allows a wrapped chain when the chain is left loose, so a person can pull on it if needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא supports the idea that a wrapped chain can be allowed, which leans toward רב הונא. It adds a condition: the wrapping must leave the chain ready to be used for leading. That way the chain is still working gear and not a mere burden.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
In order to be led or pulled

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
They go out wrapped, so as to be led.
phrases.notes: The chain is wound loosely so that it can still be pulled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source on the רב הונא and שמואל dispute about wrapped chains.
steps.raayaObject: That a wrapped chain can be permitted, in line with רב הונא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that allows a chain wrapped loosely so the animal can be led.

steps.title: רב יוסף saw רב הונא's calves with wrapped halters
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף reports that the calves of רב הונא's household went out on שבת with their halters wrapped around their necks.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: I saw the calves of רב הונא's household go out on שבת with their halters wrapped.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף tells what he saw. רב הונא's own calves went out on שבת with their halters wrapped, which matches רב הונא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that רב הונא acted on his own ruling in real life. Seeing a sage's practice was treated as strong support that he truly held this as the law.

keyTerms.meaning: I saw
Calves
Halter or bit, with its reins

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: חֲזֵינָא לְהוּ לְעִיגְלֵי דְּבֵי רַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: I saw the calves of the house of Rav Huna
going out with their halters wrapped, on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: חֲזֵינָא לְהוּ לְעִיגְלֵי דְּבֵי רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a report of actual practice to support רב הונא.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's view that wrapped halters are permitted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: An eyewitness report of the practice in רב הונא's own household.

steps.title: Report: the mules of רבי's household went out with halters
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports in the name of רבי חנינא that the mules of רבי's household went out on שבת with their halters.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came from ארץ ישראל, he said in the name of רבי חנינא: The mules of רבי's household go out with their halters on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי brings a report from ארץ ישראל about the mules of רבי יהודה הנשיא's household. The report does not say how the halters were worn, and this sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The practice of רבי's household carries great weight. But the report leaves out the one detail that matters for our dispute: whether the halters were wrapped or held.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
Mules
The household of רבי יהודה הנשיא

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came
he said that Rabbi Ḥanina said:
The mules of the house of Rabbi
go out with their halters on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings another report of practice, this time without the key detail.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The mules of רבי's household went out on שבת with their halters.

steps.title: Were the mules' halters wrapped or held?
steps.stepSummary: The scholars ask whether the halters in רב דימי's report were wrapped around the necks or used to lead the mules.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: Were they wrapped, or were they led?
steps.whatsHappening: The scholars ask what רב דימי's report meant. Were the halters wrapped around the mules' necks, or were people leading the mules by them?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the halters were wrapped, the report supports רב הונא against שמואל. If the mules were led, the report fits both views and settles nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: They asked (a question raised among the scholars)

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
Wrapped, or led?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the missing detail in the report of step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the halters of רבי's mules were wrapped or used for leading.

steps.title: A fuller report: the halters were wrapped
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר יהודה reports the same statement of רבי חנינא with the detail that the halters were wrapped.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: When רב שמואל בר יהודה came, he said in the name of רבי חנינא: The mules of רבי's household go out with their halters wrapped on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a second version of the same report. This version adds the word 'wrapped.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fuller version shows that רבי's household let mules go out with wrapped halters. That backs רב הונא's view, along with the ברייתא and רב יוסף's report.

keyTerms.meaning: Wrapped (the same word as כרוכין)

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא allows a chain or halter either wrapped or used for leading. שמואל allows only leading. The ברייתא, the practice in רב הונא's home, and the practice in רבי's home all show that wrapped halters were permitted.

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: When Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda came
he said that Rabbi Ḥanina said:
The mules of the house of Rabbi
go out with their halters wrapped on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, כִּי אֲתָא רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה אֲמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23 with a fuller version of the report.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The halters were wrapped, which supports רב הונא.

steps.title: The Sages argue that רב שמואל בר יהודה's report is unnecessary
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן tell רב אסי that רב שמואל בר יהודה's report adds nothing new. Their reasoning is that רב דימי's report must already be about wrapped halters. If רב דימי meant halters used for leading, his report would only repeat what we know from רב יהודה in the name of שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages said before רב אסי: רב שמואל בר יהודה's statement is not needed, because we can learn it from רב דימי's. Why? If you thought רב דימי was talking about mules being led by the halter, we would already know that from what רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: The Sages challenge step 24. They say the extra report about wrapped halters is redundant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their argument has three links. First, רב דימי cannot be talking about leading, because רב יהודה's teaching already allows that. So רב דימי must mean wrapped halters, which makes רב שמואל בר יהודה's version add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not needed; it is redundant.
It comes out from; it can be learned from.
If it would enter your mind; if you were to think.
Pulled or led by the halter.

steps.confusionAlert: Nobody here is disputing the הלכה. The Sages are asking whether a particular report adds anything new. In the גמרא's view, a teaching that adds nothing should not need to be said.

phrases.english: The Sages said it before Rav Asi:

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה לָא צְרִיכָא,
phrases.english: That statement of Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda is not necessary,
it can be derived from Rav Dimi's statement.
For if it would enter your mind
that Rav Dimi was saying "pulled" (led by the halter),
phrases.notes: In other words, that רב דימי's mules were being led by their halters.

phrases.english: that could already be derived from what Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the report quoted in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שמואל בר יהודה's report that the halters were wrapped.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A report about leading would repeat רב יהודה's teaching, so רב דימי must mean wrapped halters. That makes רב שמואל בר יהודה's report redundant.

steps.title: The teaching of רב יהודה in the name of שמואל about four animals and the halter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the earlier source the Sages relied on. The students in front of רבי asked whether one animal may go out with another animal's gear. רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי answered in his father's name that four animals, including the mule, may go out with an אפסר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The students in front of רבי mixed up the cases and asked, 'What is the law if one animal goes out with the item meant for another animal?' רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי said before him: 'This is what my father said: four animals may go out with a halter. They are the horse, the mule, the camel, and the donkey.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source the Sages mentioned. It shows that a mule being led by its halter was already known to be permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה lists certain gear for certain animals, so the students asked whether one animal may use another animal's gear. רבי יוסי's answer includes the mule among the animals that may go out with an אפסר used for leading. That is why the Sages said a report about leading mules would teach nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: Switching, meaning they mixed up which gear goes with which animal.
This animal's item on that animal.
A halter or bridle used to lead an animal.
Mule.

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
They were switching the cases before Rabbi,
and asking: what is the law of this animal going out with that animal's item?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לְפָנָיו רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei said before him,
"This is what my father said:
four animals may go out with a halter:
the horse, the mule, the camel, and the donkey."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the source the Sages pointed to in step 25.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that leading a mule by its halter is already known to be permitted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי, quoting his father, as transmitted by רב יהודה in the name of שמואל.

steps.title: רב אסי explains why רב דימי's report is needed
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי answers that every report is needed. From רב יהודה's report alone, we might think רבי heard the ruling but did not accept it. רב דימי's report shows that רבי's own mules actually went out that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said to them: Both reports are needed. If we only had רב יהודה's report, I would have said that רבי ישמעאל told this to רבי, but רבי did not accept it from him. So רב דימי's report teaches us that רבי did accept it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי starts his answer by showing what רב דימי's report adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה's report only says the ruling was spoken in front of רבי. It does not say רבי agreed. רב דימי's report describes what was actually done in רבי's household, and that shows רבי accepted the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed.
I would have thought; the mistaken assumption we might have made.
He accepted it from him.
It teaches us something new.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב אַסִּי: אִיצְטְרִיךְ לְהוּ.
phrases.english: Rav Asi said to them: They are needed.
For if we derived it only from Rav Yehuda's statement,
I would have said:
he said it before him, but Rabbi did not accept it from him.
So Rav Dimi's statement teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב אַסִּי: אִיצְטְרִיךְ לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 25 by showing that רב דימי's report adds something.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא (showing that each source is needed)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי heard the ruling but did not accept it.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב דימי's report shows that רבי accepted the ruling in practice.

steps.title: רב אסי explains why the report about wrapped halters is needed
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי continues his answer. From רב דימי's report alone, we might think only a halter used for leading is allowed. רב שמואל בר רב יהודה's report shows that a halter wrapped around the neck is allowed too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if we only had רב דימי's report, I would have said that this applies only when the mules are led by the halter, but a halter wrapped around the neck is not allowed. So רב שמואל בר רב יהודה's report teaches us that wrapped halters are allowed too.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי finishes his answer by showing that רב שמואל בר רב יהודה's report also adds something. With that, the challenge from step 25 is fully answered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רב אסי reads רב דימי's report as being about leading. Read that way, it might seem to allow only halters used for leading. The second report adds that wrapping the halter is permitted as well.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply only to; this is limited to.
Wrapped around the animal's neck.

steps.whatToRemember: Each report teaches its own point. רב יהודה's report gives the ruling. רב דימי's report shows that רבי accepted it in practice. רב שמואל בר רב יהודה's report shows that even a wrapped halter is permitted.

phrases.english: And if we had only Rav Dimi's statement, I would have said:
this applies only when they are pulled (led by the halter),
but when the halters are wrapped, no.

phrases.aramaic: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: So Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yehuda's statement teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב אסי's answer that began in step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא (showing that each source is needed)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a halter used for leading is permitted, not a wrapped one.
steps.terutzMaskana: A halter wrapped around the neck is also permitted.

steps.title: The משנה: animal chains may be purified on the animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of our משנה: one may sprinkle purifying water on the animals' chains and immerse them right where they are.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may sprinkle purifying water on them and immerse them in their place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to our משנה and quotes the line about animal chains. It is setting up a question on this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said animals that normally wear chains may go out with them. Now it adds that if the chains became טמא, they can be made טהור by sprinkling and immersion without taking them off. This line assumes the chains can become טמא in the first place, and that assumption is what the גמרא will question next.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkle. Here it means sprinkling purifying water (מֵי חַטָּאת) to remove טומאת מת.
Immerse them, in a מקוה, to purify them.
In their place. This means while they are still on the animal.

phrases.english: And one may sprinkle on them
phrases.notes: The sprinkling of purifying water used for טומאת מת.

phrases.english: and immerse them in their place.
phrases.notes: While the chains are still on the animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The halter discussion ended in step 28. Now the גמרא moves on to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Animal chains that became טמא may be purified by sprinkling and immersion while still on the animal.

steps.title: Can animal chains really become impure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the משנה means that these chains are the kind of object that can become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this to say that they are able to become impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out what the משנה seems to assume: if the chains need purifying, they must be able to become טמא. It is getting ready to show that this assumption is hard to accept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You can only purify something that was able to become טמא. So the line in the משנה implies that animal chains are בני קבולי טומאה. The question is worded as a question, but it works as the opening of a challenge, which the next step supports with a source.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say? A phrase that draws an implication from a source, usually before challenging it.
Able to receive טומאה. Something that can become impure.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as a request for information. The word לְמֵימְרָא signals that the גמרא finds the implication difficult, and the next step brings the source that makes it difficult.

phrases.english: Is this to say
phrases.notes: The גמרא is drawing a conclusion here that it's about to challenge.

phrases.english: that they are capable of receiving impurity?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It draws out what step 29 assumes and starts to challenge it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's assumption that animal chains can become טמא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Purifying something only makes sense if it can become טמא. But there is a source suggesting that ornaments worn by animals cannot become טמא.

steps.title: The ring משנה: a person's ring versus an animal's ring
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a משנה. A person's ring can become טמא, but it sets apart animal rings, utensil rings, and all other rings. The quote continues into the next passage.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in a משנה: A ring of a person is impure, but a ring of an animal, and rings of utensils, and all other rings —
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to support its challenge. This passage ends in the middle of the quote, so the ruling about animal rings comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה sets up a contrast. A ring worn by a person is טמאה, meaning it can become impure. Animal rings, utensil rings, and other rings are listed separately, which hints that they are treated differently, namely that they cannot become impure. If so, an animal's chain should also not be able to become טמא, and that clashes with our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: A ring.
Impure. Here it means able to become impure.
An animal.

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is unfinished. The ruling for animal and utensil rings, that they cannot become impure, comes at the start of the next passage.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a mishnah:
A ring of a person is impure,
phrases.notes: It is a human ornament, so it can become impure.

phrases.english: but the ring of an animal, and of utensils,
and all other rings —
phrases.notes: The quote continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It supplies the source behind the challenge raised in step 30.
steps.raayaObject: That ornaments worn by animals cannot become טמא, which contradicts our משנה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה about rings that contrasts a person's ring (טמאה) with animal, utensil, and other rings.
